questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 41. Define Biodiversity and list factors that threaten biodiversity. [2 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms (genes, species and ecosystems) in an area or on Earth.
Threats: habitat destruction (deforestation, urbanization), pollution, overexploitation (overhunting, overfishing), invasive species, climate change, disease.

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question:
42. Describe the uses of the following tools in genetic engineering: ......[4 Marks]
  a. Restriction enzyme
  b. Gene cloning
questions.answer_guide:
a. Restriction enzymes act as “molecular scissors”: they cut DNA at specific base sequences so a desired gene can be removed or a vector opened.
b. Gene cloning makes many identical copies of a gene (e.g. inserted into a plasmid and multiplied in bacteria), used to produce proteins such as insulin and for research.

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 44. Explain briefly the difference between fast-twitch and slow twitch muscles? ..... [4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
Slow-twitch fibres contract slowly, use aerobic respiration, have many mitochondria and myoglobin (red), and resist fatigue – used for endurance (e.g. long-distance running).
Fast-twitch fibres contract quickly and powerfully, rely mainly on anaerobic respiration, have fewer mitochondria (white) and tire quickly – used for short bursts (e.g. sprinting, lifting).

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 46. A student fell while playing football and broken his leg. Describe the process that body undergoes to repair the broken bone? .......... [4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
1. Haematoma (blood clot) forms at the break.
2. A soft callus of fibrocartilage forms to bridge the gap.
3. Osteoblasts replace it with a hard bony callus.
4. Remodelling by osteoclasts and osteoblasts restores the original bone shape.

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 47. Compare the structure of DNA and RNA, highlighting their similarities and differences..... [4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
Similarities: both are nucleic acids made of nucleotides (sugar, phosphate, base); both contain A, G and C; both carry genetic information.
Differences: DNA is double-stranded, RNA single-stranded; DNA has deoxyribose sugar, RNA ribose; DNA has thymine, RNA has uracil; DNA is mainly in the nucleus, RNA also in the cytoplasm.

   (Diagram: neuron with labels 1–6 – cell body, dendrites, axon, myelin sheath, node, axon terminals)
  a. Name the parts of neurons labeled 1, 2,3 and 5 ? .[2 Marks]
  b. Describe the function of the parts 2 and 3 ......[2 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
a. 1 – cell body (with nucleus); 2 – dendrites; 3 – axon; 5 – myelin sheath / node of Ranvier (6 – axon terminals)
b. Dendrites (2) receive impulses from other neurons and carry them to the cell body; the axon (3) carries impulses away from the cell body to other cells. [Check against the official key.]

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 50. Briefly explain the difference between lichens and mychorrhiza........[4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
A lichen is a mutualistic association between a fungus and an alga (or cyanobacterium): the alga makes food by photosynthesis and the fungus provides shelter, water and minerals.
Mycorrhiza is a mutualistic association between a fungus and the roots of a plant: the fungus helps the roots absorb water and minerals and receives sugars from the plant.

52. Hemophilia is caused by an X-linked recessive gene. If a hemophiliac man marries a carrier woman:
  a. What is the probability that their son will have hemophilia? ........ [2 marks]
  b. What is the probability that their daughter will have hemophilia?...[2 Marks ]
  c. What is the probability that their daughter will be carrier? .......[2 Marks ]
questions.answer_guide:

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 53. Explain how intracellular enzymes differ from extracellular enzymes........ [4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide: Intracellular enzymes work inside the cell where they are made (e.g. respiratory enzymes, catalase). Extracellular enzymes are secreted out of the cell and work outside it (e.g. digestive enzymes such as amylase and pepsin in the gut).

   (Diagram: digestive tract with labels A–E)
  a. Name the parts labeled A, B, C,D and E. ..........[2 Marks]
  b. State the function of the part labeled D in the digestive system..........[2 Marks]
questions.answer_guide:
a. Likely: A – liver; B – small intestine; C – large intestine (colon); D – oesophagus/stomach; E – stomach/pancreas (labels are hard to read in the scan).

questions.section: Section B: Structural Questions [60 Marks]
questions.question: 55. Briefly explain the importance of protista....... [4 Marks]
questions.answer_guide: Algae (protists) produce much of the world's oxygen by photosynthesis; they form the base of aquatic food chains (plankton); some decompose dead matter and recycle nutrients; some are used in industry (agar, diatomite) and research; some cause diseases (malaria, amoebic dysentery), so studying them helps medicine.
